rules.statement: The financial statements (stato patrimoniale, conto economico, rendiconto finanziario, nota integrativa) shall be drawn up clearly and shall give a true and fair view of the company's financial position and result for the year.

If the information required by law is insufficient to give a true and fair view, supplementary information must be provided; in exceptional cases a statutory provision must be departed from and the departure explained in the notes.
The financial statements shall be expressed in euro; figures may be rounded to the euro and the notes may be drawn up in thousands of euro.
Valuation of items shall be made prudently and on a going-concern basis, taking account of the economic function of the asset or liability considered.
Income and charges shall be accounted for on an accruals basis (competenza economica) regardless of the date of receipt or payment.
Only profits realised at the balance-sheet date may be recognised, while foreseeable risks and losses pertaining to the year shall be recorded even if known after year-end.
Valuation criteria shall not be changed from one financial year to the next; departures are permitted only in exceptional cases and must be justified in the notes.
Items shall be recognised and presented having regard to the substance of the transaction or contract.

The balance sheet shall follow the statutory layout, with assets classified as crediti verso soci, immobilizzazioni, attivo circolante and ratei e risconti, and liabilities/equity as patrimonio netto, fondi per rischi e oneri, TFR, debiti and ratei e risconti.

The income statement shall follow the statutory by-nature layout in scalar form, with sections A (valore della produzione), B (costi della produzione), C (proventi e oneri finanziari) and D (rettifiche di valore di attività finanziarie).

The cash-flow statement (rendiconto finanziario) shall report the amount and composition of cash and cash equivalents and the cash flows from operating, investing and financing activities for the year.
Fixed assets shall be recorded at acquisition or production cost, including accessory charges and directly attributable production costs.
The cost of fixed assets with a limited useful life shall be systematically depreciated each year in relation to their residual useful life.
A fixed asset showing a durable loss of value lower than its carrying amount shall be written down to that lower value; the write-down shall be reversed if the reasons for it cease to exist.

Development costs with multi-year utility may be capitalised with consent of the board of statutory auditors and amortised over their useful life; until fully amortised, dividends may be distributed only if sufficient distributable reserves remain.

Goodwill may be recorded only if acquired for consideration and shall be amortised over its useful life; where useful life cannot be reliably estimated it shall be amortised over a period not exceeding ten years.
Receivables and payables shall be measured at amortised cost taking account of the time factor and, for receivables, their presumed realisable value.
Inventories shall be measured at the lower of acquisition or production cost and the realisable value derivable from market conditions.
Cost of fungible inventories may be computed using weighted-average cost or the FIFO or LIFO assumptions; any difference from current cost at year-end shall be disclosed in the notes.
Derivative financial instruments shall be measured at fair value, with changes recognised in the income statement or, for qualifying cash-flow hedges, in an equity reserve.

The notes (nota integrativa) shall disclose the valuation criteria applied and the further information items listed in art. 2427 (movements of fixed assets, equity composition, related-party transactions, etc.).
Companies not exceeding two of the three size thresholds may draw up an abbreviated balance sheet and income statement, aggregating certain items and omitting the cash-flow statement.
Micro-enterprises not exceeding the statutory thresholds may be exempted from the cash-flow statement and the notes provided the relevant information is given at the foot of the balance sheet.
Accounting books, records and the originals of correspondence and supporting documents shall be retained for ten years from the date of the last entry.
Financial statements shall be prepared on a going-concern, accruals and prudence basis, applying the postulates of relevance and substance over form set out in OIC 11.
The composition and statutory layout of the balance sheet, income statement, cash-flow statement and notes shall follow the schemes and classification rules of OIC 12.
Inventories of raw materials, work-in-progress, semi-finished and finished goods shall be measured at the lower of cost (specific or weighted-average/FIFO/LIFO) and net realisable value per OIC 13.
Receivables shall be measured at amortised cost using the effective-interest method, adjusted to presumed realisable value through an allowance for doubtful accounts per OIC 15.
Tangible fixed assets shall be recorded at cost, depreciated systematically over their useful life by component where significant, and written down for durable impairment per OIC 16.
Intangible fixed assets shall be capitalised at cost only where they meet recognition criteria and amortised systematically over their useful life per OIC 24.

Impairment losses on tangible and intangible fixed assets shall be recognised when the recoverable amount (value in use or fair value less costs to sell) falls durably below carrying amount per OIC 9.

Revenue from the sale of goods and rendering of services shall be recognised by segmenting the contract into unit elements and recognising each when the related obligation is satisfied, net of variable consideration, per OIC 34.
OIC 34 (Ricavi) applies to financial statements for years beginning on or after 1 January 2024.
Current and deferred income taxes shall be recognised, with deferred tax assets recognised only to the extent their recovery is reasonably certain, per OIC 25.
Provisions for risks and charges shall be recognised for probable liabilities of uncertain timing or amount, measured at the best estimate of the outflow, per OIC 31.
VAT-registered businesses shall issue and transmit invoices electronically in FatturaPA XML format through the Sistema di Interscambio (SdI) for B2B and B2C transactions.
The annual accounts shall give a true and fair view (imagen fiel) of the equity, financial position and results of the undertaking in accordance with the conceptual framework of the PGC.
Transactions shall be recognised on an accrual basis (principio de devengo), allocating income and expenses to the period to which they relate irrespective of payment dates.

rules.source: PGC Marco Conceptual — empresa en funcionamiento
rules.statement: The accounts shall be prepared on a going-concern basis (empresa en funcionamiento) unless the intention or necessity to liquidate exists.
Prudence (prudencia) shall be exercised: only realised profits at year-end are recognised, while foreseeable risks and losses are recorded as soon as known.

rules.source: PGC Marco Conceptual — primacía del fondo económico
rules.statement: Transactions shall be accounted for according to their economic substance and not merely their legal form (primacía del fondo económico sobre la forma).

rules.source: PGC norma 2ª de registro y valoración
rules.statement: Property, plant and equipment (inmovilizado material) shall be measured initially at acquisition price or production cost and subsequently at cost less accumulated depreciation and impairment.

rules.source: PGC norma 5ª de registro y valoración
rules.statement: Intangible assets (inmovilizado intangible) shall be recognised only where they meet the identifiability criterion and measured at cost less amortisation and impairment.
Goodwill (fondo de comercio) shall be recognised only when acquired for consideration and amortised over its useful life, presumed to be ten years unless proven otherwise.

rules.source: PGC norma 9ª de registro y valoración
rules.statement: Financial instruments shall be classified and measured according to norma 9ª, with most financial assets at amortised cost or fair value depending on category.

rules.source: PGC norma 10ª de registro y valoración
rules.statement: Inventories (existencias) shall be measured at the lower of cost (using weighted-average or FIFO) and net realisable value.

rules.source: PGC norma 14ª de registro y valoración
rules.statement: Revenue from the sale of goods and rendering of services (ingresos por ventas y prestación de servicios) shall be recognised when control is transferred to the customer, measured at the consideration expected, per the revised norma 14ª.
The ICAC resolution of 10 February 2021 develops norma 14ª revenue recognition aligned with the five-step model, applicable to years beginning on or after 1 January 2021.
Accounts should be coded according to the PGC chart of accounts (cuadro de cuentas), classified in seven groups (1 financiación básica … 7 ventas e ingresos).
The annual accounts comprise the balance, profit-and-loss account, statement of changes in equity, cash-flow statement and notes (memoria), drawn up on the normal model.
Undertakings within the size thresholds may use the abbreviated models of balance, profit-and-loss account and notes and are exempt from the cash-flow statement.
Small and medium-sized undertakings within the thresholds may apply the simplified PGC de PYMES with reduced recognition, valuation and disclosure requirements.
Business operators shall retain their books, correspondence, documentation and supporting records, duly ordered, for six years from the last entry made in the books.
Spain will require structured electronic invoicing for all B2B transactions, phased in by company size, under the Crea y Crece law and its implementing regulation.
Billing software shall produce tamper-evident, chained invoice records meeting the VERI*FACTU requirements; the obligation applies from 1 January 2027 for entities outside the SII (verify).
In the Basque Country and Navarre, invoicing software shall generate signed, chained TicketBAI records transmitted to the regional tax authority.
Large taxpayers and other obliged entities shall submit VAT ledger records electronically to the AEAT in near real time under the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información).

rules.source: Code de droit économique art. III.86
rules.statement: Undertakings shall retain their books and supporting documents, methodically filed, for seven years counted from 1 January of the year following their closing.

rules.source: Code de droit économique art. III.86 (verify)
rules.statement: Every accounting entry shall be supported by a dated supporting document bearing an index reference to it.
Undertakings shall keep accounts using the standardised minimum chart of accounts (PCMN/MAR), with classes 1–5 for the balance sheet and classes 6–7 for the income statement.

rules.source: AR exécution Code des sociétés et des associations (CAR)
rules.statement: The annual accounts shall give a true and fair view (image fidèle) of the undertaking's assets, financial position and results.
Each undertaking shall determine and consistently apply valuation rules, measuring assets at acquisition cost less depreciation and writing down assets whose value is durably lower.
Valuation shall be made prudently, on a going-concern basis and applying the accruals principle, recognising charges and risks pertaining to the year even if known after year-end.
Annual accounts shall be drawn up on the standard NBB model (full, abbreviated or micro) according to the undertaking's size category.
Companies shall file their annual accounts with the National Bank of Belgium's Central Balance Sheet Office within thirty days of approval and at most seven months after year-end.
In the absence of an explicit legal rule, the accounting treatment recommended in the relevant CNC/CBN opinion (avis) should be applied.
Undertakings are advised to use the asset-and-liability templates issued by the NBB and the minimum classification of the standardised chart of accounts per CBN opinion 2020/15.
VAT-registered enterprises shall issue and receive structured electronic invoices via Peppol for B2B transactions from 1 January 2026.
Undertakings shall be able to produce the SAF-T (PT) standard audit file; the accounting SAF-T submission for tax year 2026 is postponed to 2027 (verify).
Certified billing software shall generate the SAF-T (PT) billing file and report invoices to the Autoridade Tributária (e-Fatura), with QR-code and ATCUD on invoices.
Accounting books, records and supporting documents shall be retained for ten years.
Taxpayers shall submit the SAF-T standard audit file via Declaration D406, covering general ledger, accounts receivable/payable, fixed assets and inventory data.
Taxable persons shall issue B2B invoices through the national RO e-Factura system in the structured national format.
Invoice data shall be reported to the tax authority in real time through the Online Számla (RTIR) system immediately upon issue.
Hungary is preparing a SAF-T obligation; it is not yet mandatory but is expected to be required in the near future (verify).
Businesses shall transmit revenue and expense records and accounting summaries electronically to the AADE through the myDATA platform.
Greece is introducing mandatory B2B electronic invoicing integrated with the myDATA platform (verify timeline).
VAT payers shall submit their issued and received invoice registers electronically to the tax authority through the i.SAF subsystem.
Undertakings shall be able to produce the i.SAF-T standard accounting file with general-ledger and transaction data on request of the tax authority.
Bookkeeping entities shall be able to produce the SAF-T Financial standard file on request from the tax administration.
Primary accounting records shall be retained for at least five years after the end of the financial year.
Undertakings shall be able to provide a SAF-T export of accounting data on demand during a tax audit.
Books, records and supporting documents shall be retained for seven years.
Undertakings keeping computerised accounts shall be able to produce the FAIA (Fichier d'Audit Informatisé AED) SAF-T file on request of the tax authority.
Accounting books and supporting documents shall be retained for ten years.
Undertakings keeping computerised accounts shall produce the Fichier des Écritures Comptables (FEC) in the prescribed format at the start of a tax audit.
All companies shall be able to receive structured electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; large and intermediate taxpayers shall also issue them from that date, SMEs from 1 September 2027.
Accounting documents and supporting records shall be retained for ten years.
Taxable persons shall issue structured B2B invoices through the national e-invoicing system KSeF, with large taxpayers obliged from 1 February 2026 and others phased thereafter.
Taxpayers shall submit SAF-T structures (JPK_VAT and other JPK files) to the tax authority periodically or on demand.
Books, inventories, financial statements and booking vouchers shall be retained for ten years (commercial letters for six years).

Domestic B2B invoices shall be issued as structured electronic invoices (EN 16931, e.g. XRechnung/ZUGFeRD); all businesses must be able to receive them from 1 January 2025, with issuance phased through 2028.
Accounting records shall be retained for seven years (ten years for immovable-property records).
Bookkeeping systems shall be able to export accounting data in the Danish SAF-T format under the digital bookkeeping requirements.
Bulgaria is introducing SAF-T reporting phased from 2026, starting with the largest taxpayers (verify).
For tax purposes, accounting records shall be retained until the time-limit for tax assessment expires (generally five years from filing), in addition to the ten-year civil-law period.
